text:
taylor (support): FYI — Acme Health opened an escalation: they saw intermittent 403s for inference calls and reported missing audit entries after a KMS rotation earlier today. They want scope + timeline for affected logs and whether we need to notify customers.
mike (eng): Short summary from infra: KMS rotation executed at 2026-03-17T08:12Z. There was a mapping sync failure in the HSM agent for ~7 minutes (08:12:20–08:19:30 UTC) that caused decrypts to fail and audit-log write errors. We retried and backfilled most entries, but there are gaps. Repro snippet below.
```
$ ./kms-rotate --key-id old-key --new-key new-key --apply
INFO 08:12:20 rotation started
ERROR 08:13:01 hsm-agent decrypt failed key_not_found
WARN 08:18:45 audit-log write failed: upstream timeout
INFO 08:19:30 mapping sync completed; retries succeeded
```

sara (security): Can you confirm which log types were impacted (auth events, request metadata, payloads)? Need to know if payloads or any customer-provided content were ever dropped vs delayed. Also need the list of customers with events in that window.
ana (typo fixed) — oops, pinging correct person: ana (privacy): If any logs containing request metadata or identifiers are permanently lost we need to follow our notification policy. Please provide exact time window and count. We'll need to prepare the notification template and log the retention/legal rationale.
josh (legal): Quick guidance: notification should include time window, impact (what types of logs), mitigation steps (retries/backfill done), and contact for support. If no content payloads were exposed or lost, we can phrase it as a service degradation with possible missing audit entries. Legal review required before sending.
mike (eng): Quick notes on repro and mitigation steps we ran:

1) Detected mapping mismatch in HSM agent, root cause: race in key rotation handler.
2) Immediate mitigation: restarted hsm-agent on affected hosts, triggered explicit mapping sync.
3) Backfill: replays from s3/audit-buffer, ~92% of missing entries re-ingested.

Sample command used for backfill:
```
$ python infra/tools/backfill_audit.py --start 2026-03-17T08:12:00Z --end 2026-03-17T08:20:00Z --source s3://audit-buffer/2026-03-17
Backfilled 1841 entries, skipped 152 duplicates
```

taylor (support): Customer also mentioned a weird duplicate billing event earlier this morning — are billing logs affected? We need to tell them definitively in the comms.
mike (eng): Billing ingestion pipeline runs downstream of a separate collector; we did not observe failures there. I checked the billing topic offsets for that window — no gaps or duplicate publish. Likely unrelated, but we'll keep watching.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0317-12 · Severity: P2 · Assigned: mike (eng), sara (security) · Channel: #incidents
ana (correction): ana (privacy): I'll draft a notification template with placeholders. josh, want to loop you in for wording. Will wait for the customer list + final confirmation of which log classes were permanently lost vs backfilled.
josh (legal): ack. Once we have precise bucket counts and a short impact statement, legal sign-off should be quick.
mike (eng): Actionable items I can commit to in the next 2 hours: produce list of affected customers + exact time windows; provide counts for missing vs backfilled entries; confirm whether any payloads (request bodies) were part of audit entries lost.

sara (security): I'll validate whether any auth tokens or secrets could have been retrievable from the dropped logs — preliminary look says no, but I'll confirm.
 
taylor (support): Customer asked for ETA on notification: can we share a draft by EOD today? I'll hold off external comms until legal/priv/sec sign-off. @mike @sara please ping me in this thread when you have the customer list.
mike (eng): on it :eyes:
sara (security): on it :spiral_calendar:
 
taylor (support): Thanks — I will keep Acme Health updated that we're investigating and will provide a timeline within 2 hours.
